transcript.heading: News Report One (American Female)
paras: The government of Canada announced new immigration rules yesterday that will make it easier for international students to obtain work permits after graduation. Starting in January, international students who complete a two-year program at a Canadian post-secondary institution will be eligible for a three-year open work permit, an increase from the current two-year limit. Additionally, students in certain high-demand fields such as healthcare, technology, and skilled trades will be able to apply for permanent residency directly after graduation without requiring a job offer. Immigration Minister Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the changes are designed to help Canada attract and retain global talent as the country faces labor shortages in key sectors. The announcement has been welcomed by universities across the country, which have seen international student enrollment grow by 40 percent over the past five years. However, some critics argue that the new rules could put additional pressure on housing markets in major cities like Toronto and Vancouver, where rental costs have already risen sharply. The government says it is working with provincial and municipal partners to address housing concerns as part of the immigration strategy.

transcript.heading: News Report Two (British Male)
paras: The World Health Organization has released new guidelines recommending that children aged 5 to 18 limit recreational screen time to no more than two hours per day, and that children under 5 should have no more than one hour. The guidelines also emphasize that screens should be avoided entirely for children under one year old. The recommendations are based on a comprehensive review of research linking excessive screen use to a range of health problems in young people, including poor sleep quality, reduced physical activity, eye strain, and increased risk of anxiety and depression. The WHO says that while educational screen time can be valuable, the recreational use of smartphones, tablets, and video games often displaces healthier activities such as outdoor play, face-to-face social interaction, and sleep. The guidelines also encourage parents to establish screen-free zones in the home, particularly during meals and in bedrooms, and to model healthy screen habits themselves. Several countries have already incorporated similar recommendations into their national public health policies.
Questions 4 and 5 are based on the news report you have just heard. (British Female)

5. What does the WHO say about parents regarding screen habits?

transcript.heading: News Report Three (American Male)
paras: A medical technology company based in Boston has received approval from health regulators for a new wearable device that can continuously monitor blood glucose levels without requiring finger pricks. The device, worn on the upper arm like a small patch, uses a tiny sensor that measures glucose levels through the skin and transmits readings wirelessly to a smartphone app. Unlike existing continuous glucose monitors, this new model does not require calibration with blood samples and can be worn for up to 30 days before replacement. The company says the device is 95 percent accurate compared to traditional blood tests and will be available by prescription starting next spring, with an expected cost of about 50 dollars per month. While primarily designed for people with diabetes, the company is also exploring applications for weight management and sports performance. Health experts say the technology could significantly improve quality of life for millions of people who need to monitor their blood sugar regularly.

transcript.heading: Conversation One (British Female + American Male)
paras: Woman (Karen): Good morning, Michael. Thank you for coming in today. I'm Karen, the marketing director. Please have a seat. Did you find our office easily?
Man (Michael): Good morning, Karen. Yes, thank you—the directions on your website were very clear. I actually took the subway, and it's just a five-minute walk from the station. Very convenient.

Woman: Great to hear. So, I've reviewed your resume, and I must say your coursework in digital marketing looks impressive. I see you're completing your business degree this semester. Can you tell me a bit about why you're interested in this marketing internship?

Man: Absolutely. I've been focusing on digital marketing and social media strategy in my classes, and I've been following your company's campaigns for a while now. I particularly loved the "Sustainable Futures" campaign you ran last quarter—the way you integrated user-generated content was really clever. I'm eager to get hands-on experience working on real projects rather than just case studies.

Woman: That's wonderful to hear. That campaign actually won a regional marketing award, so I'm glad it caught your attention. This internship will involve supporting our social media team, helping draft content, analyzing engagement metrics, and assisting with event planning. Do you have any experience with social media management tools or analytics?

Man: In my digital marketing class, we worked with Hootsuite for scheduling posts and Google Analytics to track website traffic. I also run a small Instagram account for a student club I'm in, which has grown to about 2,000 followers over the past year. I've had to plan content calendars and engage with our audience there.

Woman: That's excellent practical experience. Now, this is a paid internship—18 dollars an hour, 20 hours per week during the semester. We're flexible with scheduling around classes, but we do need someone who can commit to at least two full weekdays in the office. Would that work for your class schedule?
Man: Yes, I have classes on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, so I can work all day Tuesdays and Thursdays, and I could also do Friday afternoons if needed.

Woman: Perfect. The internship runs for 12 weeks from September through November, with the possibility of extending into the spring semester for the right candidate. We also try to offer full-time positions to our top interns after graduation. Do you have any questions for me about the role?
Man: Yes, actually—what would a typical day look like for an intern on your team? And will there be opportunities to work on cross-functional projects with other departments?

transcript.heading: Conversation Two (American Female + British Male)
paras: Woman (Nurse): Good afternoon, Riverside Medical Clinic. How may I help you?
Man (Paul): Hello, I'd like to make an appointment to see Dr. Peterson, please. I've been having some persistent headaches and dizziness over the past week, and I'd like to get it checked out.
Woman: I'm sorry to hear that. Have you been a patient here before?
Man: Yes, I came in last month for my annual physical. My last name is Harrison—Paul Harrison.
Woman: Let me pull up your record... Here you are, Paul Harrison. Dr. Peterson has availability this Thursday at 2:30 PM, or next Monday at 10:00 AM. Would either of those work for you?
Man: I have a work meeting Thursday afternoon that I can't reschedule. Is there anything available earlier this week, maybe Wednesday?

Woman: Let me check... Dr. Peterson is fully booked Wednesday, but we do have a cancellation for tomorrow morning at 9:15 AM with Dr. Thompson. Would you be comfortable seeing a different doctor? Dr. Thompson is also excellent and specializes in headaches and neurological issues, actually.

Man: Hmm, tomorrow morning is a bit short notice. Let me think... actually, the headaches have been getting worse, so tomorrow morning would be better than waiting until Monday. I can rearrange my morning schedule. Can you tell me a bit about what I should expect?

Woman: Of course. The doctor will ask you about your symptoms—when they started, how severe they are, any other symptoms you've noticed. They might check your blood pressure and do a quick neurological exam. If needed, they might refer you for further tests. Have you had any recent head injuries, or are you taking any new medications?

Man: No head injuries, but I have been under a lot of stress at work lately, and I haven't been sleeping very well. I'm not taking any medication except for occasional ibuprofen when the headaches get really bad.

Woman: That's helpful information to mention to the doctor. I'll note that in your file. Also, please try to arrive about 15 minutes early to fill out a symptom questionnaire, and bring a list of any medications you're taking, even over-the-counter ones. Would you also like me to email you the new patient forms to fill out in advance?
Man: Oh, but I'm already a patient, do I need to fill out new forms?
Woman: For symptom-specific visits, we do ask patients to complete a brief questionnaire about their current symptoms. It helps the doctor prepare. It should only take about five minutes.
Man: Alright, that makes sense. And yes, please email them to me—that will save time tomorrow. My email is paul.harrison@workmail.com.

Woman: Perfect, I'll send those right away. We'll see you tomorrow at 9:15 with Dr. Thompson. If you experience any severe symptoms like vision loss or difficulty speaking before then, please go to the emergency room immediately.
Man: I will, thank you so much for your help.

transcript.heading: Passage One (American Male)
paras: The mass shift to remote work that began during the pandemic appears to have permanently changed the modern workplace, with long-term effects that researchers are only beginning to understand. What started as an emergency measure has become the norm for millions of workers, with many companies adopting hybrid models that allow employees to work from home part of the week and in the office the rest. Studies indicate that approximately 40 percent of jobs in developed countries can be done effectively from home at least part-time, a dramatic increase from the less than 5 percent that was typical before 2020. One of the most significant findings is that remote workers often report higher productivity when working from home, citing fewer distractions from office chatter, no commute time, and greater ability to focus on deep work. Commute time savings alone add up to an average of 50 minutes per day for remote workers, time that many people redirect toward exercise, hobbies, or additional sleep. However, remote work is not without challenges. Many workers report difficulty setting boundaries between work and personal life, leading to longer working hours and increased burnout. Employees who work entirely remotely also miss out on spontaneous conversations and team bonding that can lead to creative collaborations and career advancement opportunities. Younger workers in particular may struggle with building professional networks and learning company culture from home. Researchers are finding that hybrid arrangements—typically two or three days in the office—offer the best of both worlds for many people, providing flexibility while maintaining in-person connections.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (British Female)
paras: Ocean plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing environmental challenges of our time, with an estimated 8 million tons of plastic entering the oceans annually. This plastic harms marine life, enters the food chain, and can take hundreds of years to decompose. While reducing plastic consumption and improving waste management remain essential long-term solutions, researchers and entrepreneurs are developing innovative approaches to clean up existing plastic waste. One promising technology uses specialized floating barriers that use natural ocean currents to collect plastic debris passively. These systems, deployed in ocean garbage patches, can capture plastic ranging from large pieces down to tiny microplastics without harming marine animals. Another approach involves deploying autonomous drones and underwater robots that can identify and collect plastic in coastal areas and deeper waters. Some companies are also exploring chemical recycling processes that can break down hard-to-recycle plastics into oil that can be used to make new plastic products or fuel, creating a circular economy for plastic materials. On land, many communities have installed catchment systems in rivers to prevent plastic from reaching the ocean in the first place, as rivers are the source of about 80 percent of ocean plastic. Perhaps most encouragingly, researchers have discovered several species of bacteria and fungi that can naturally break down certain types of plastic, offering hope for bioremediation solutions in the future. However, experts emphasize that cleanup technologies alone cannot solve the crisis—significant reductions in single-use plastic production and consumption are still essential.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Female)
paras: The way people read has changed dramatically over the past two decades, as digital devices have become the primary way many people consume written content. E-books, online articles, social media posts, and news apps now compete with traditional printed books and newspapers for people's attention. Research suggests that the average person reads more words per day than ever before, but the nature of that reading has shifted significantly. Instead of deep, focused reading of long texts, people now tend to engage in more scanning and skimming, hopping quickly between articles and posts. This shift has raised concerns among educators and cognitive scientists, who argue that deep reading—sustained, focused engagement with a long text—is essential for developing critical thinking, empathy, and complex reasoning skills. Studies have shown that reading on screens tends to lead to lower comprehension and retention compared to reading printed material, possibly because screens offer more distractions and encourage speed over depth. The tactile experience of reading a physical book—being able to feel the pages, see how far you've progressed, and easily flip back and forth—also appears to contribute to better understanding and memory. However, digital reading offers undeniable advantages: e-readers can store thousands of books, making reading material accessible anywhere; built-in dictionaries make it easy to look up unfamiliar words; and adjustable font sizes benefit people with visual impairments. Rather than declaring one format superior, experts recommend a balanced approach: using digital devices for quick information gathering and casual reading, while setting aside dedicated time for deep reading of printed books.
